Rashi on Yevamot 8b:11:1.hebrew: לכדר' שמעון - בפרק ד' אחים (לקמן יבמות דף כח:): ג' אחין, שנים מהם נשואין שתי אחיות או אשה ובתה, ומתו ונפלו לפני השלישי — הרי אלו חולצות ולא מתייבמו', לפי ששתיהן זקוקות לו מקדושי שני אחיו, וזיקה הוי כקצת קדושין, ואי מייבם חדא מנייהו קנסיב אחות זקוקתו בחייה, וזקוקתו הויא כאשתו; אבל חליצה בעיא, דלא אלים למיהוי כאחות אשה ממש להפטר בלא כלום. ותניא בברייתא: רבי שמעון פוטר בשתיהן מן החליצה ומן הייבום, ויליף טעמא מלצרור: בשעה שנעשו צרות זו לזו — כגון הכא דנעשו האחיות צרות זו לזו בזיקה — לא יהא לך ליקוחין אפילו באחת מהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:11:1.english: In accordance with that [statement] of Rabbi Shimon - In the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim (below, Yevamot 28b): [If there were] three brothers, two of whom were married to two sisters, or a woman and her daughter, and they died, and [the widows] fell before the third [brother for levirate marriage] — these [women] perform chalitzah and do not enter into levirate marriage, because both of them are bound to him through the betrothal of his two brothers, and the levirate bond is like partial betrothal, and if he marries one of them in levirate marriage, he is marrying the sister of his zekukah [a woman bound to him by a levirate bond] during her lifetime, and his zekukah is like his wife; however, she requires chalitzah, since [the levirate bond] is not strong enough to be like an actual wife's sister so as to be exempt without anything. And it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon exempts both of them from chalitzah and from levirate marriage, and he derives the reason from "to be a rival wife" (litzror): at the time when they become rival wives to one another — such as here, where the sisters became rival wives to one another through the levirate bond — you may not have marriage (likuchin) even with one of them.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:12:1.hebrew: א"כ - דהאי ולקחה לגופיה הוא דאתא, נימא קרא ולקח, מאי ולקחה? דמשמע דשתים נפלו לו מאחיו, ואמר רחמנא: ולקחה לאחת ולא לשתיהן. אי קרינא ולקחה בכל חדא מינייהו, שריין כל חדא מינייהו; ואי לא קרינן ולקחה בכל חדא מנייהו, כגון שהאחת ערוה, תרוייהו אסורין. וצרות צרותיהן נמי מהכא נפקא: דמשנפלה לו צרת ערוה מאחיו הראשון, ונדחית הערוה ממנו, נאסרה עליו עולמית משום אשת אח; וכשנתייבמה לאחיו השני — ולו אשה אחרת — ומת, וחזרה ונפלה לפני זה, לא קרינא בה, בזו שנאסרה עליו, ולקחה, הלכך תרוייהו אסורין, וכן לעולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:12:1.english: If so - [Meaning] that this [word] “and he shall take her” comes for itself, let the verse state, “and he shall take”; what is [the meaning of] “and he shall take her”? [It means] that it implies that two [women] fell to him [for levirate marriage] from his brother, and the Merciful One said, “and he shall take her” — [that is,] one, and not both of them. If we can apply “and he shall take her” to each one of them, each one of them is permitted; and if we cannot apply “and he shall take her” to each one of them — such as where one is a forbidden relation — both of them are prohibited. And the rival wives of their rival wives are also derived from here: for once the rival wife of a forbidden relation fell to him from his first brother, and the forbidden relation was pushed aside from him, [the rival wife] became permanently prohibited to him on account of [the prohibition of] a brother’s wife; and when she was taken in levirate marriage by his second brother — who had another wife — and he died, and she fell again before this [first brother], we cannot apply “and he shall take her” to her — to this one who had become prohibited to him; therefore, both of them are prohibited, and so on forever.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:14:1.hebrew: מלמד שמגרשה בגט ומחזירה - לאחר שנשאה, נעשית כאשתו, ואם רצה לגרשה, מגרשה בגט ואינה צריכה חליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:14:1.english: This teaches that he divorces her with a bill of divorce and remarries her - After he has married her, she becomes like his [regular] wife, and if he wishes to divorce her, he divorces her with a bill of divorce and she does not require ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:14:2.hebrew: ומחזירה - אם רצה להחזיר, ולא אמרינן מצוה רמא רחמנא עליה ועבדה, ומהשתא תיקום עליה באיסור אשת אח. להכי כתיב "ולקחה לו לאשה", דכיון שלקחה נעשית כאשתו לכל דבר:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:14:2.english: And he remarries her - If he wishes to remarry [her], and we do not say [that] the Merciful One imposed a mitzvah upon him and he fulfilled it, and from now on she should stand [forbidden] to him under the prohibition of a brother's wife. Therefore it is written, "and he shall take her to himself as a wife," for once he has taken her, she becomes like his wife in every respect.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:14:3.hebrew: בעל כרחה - שאם בא עליה יבם אפילו בעל כרחה, קנאה ויורשה ומטמא לה, ולכל דבר היא אשתו בהך ביאה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:14:3.english: Against her will - For if a yavam engages in intercourse with her even against her will, he acquires her [as his wife], and inherits her [estate], and becomes ritually impure for her [if he is a priest], and in every respect she is his wife through this act of intercourse.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:16:1.english: The court is not obligated - to bring a bull for an unwitting error [in ruling].

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:1.hebrew: למישרי צרה שלא במקום מצוה - דאי לא כתיב עליה, הוה ילפינן מלצרור דצרת אחות אשה אסורה בכל מקום:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:1.english: To permit a rival wife in a place where the mitzva is not applicable - For had “with her” not been written, we would have derived from “to be a rival” that the rival wife of a wife's sister is forbidden in all circumstances.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:2.hebrew: מאי טעמא - כלומר, היכי מידרשא היתר מהכא:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:2.english: What is the reason - That is to say: How is permission derived from here?

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:3.hebrew: במקום עליה הוא - דכתיב לצרור למיסר צרה, ולא במקום אחר:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:3.english: It is in a place of “with her” - For it is written “to be a rival wife” to prohibit a rival wife, and not in another place.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:2:1.hebrew: אימא ערוה גופה שלא במקום מצוה תשתרי - מדכתיב עליה, דקאי נמי אאחות אשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:2:1.english: Say that the forbidden relative herself, [when] not in a place of a mitzvah, should be permitted - Since it is written “upon her,” which also applies to a wife’s sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:3:1.english: As long as [she is] in her lifetime - [Throughout the lifetime of] your wife, you shall not marry her sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:1.hebrew: תרי קראי כתיבי - מעיקרא כתיב ״לצרור״, דמשמע לא היא ולא צרתה; והדר כתיב ״לגלות ערותה״, דמשמע חדא הוא דאסירא:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:1.english: Two verses are written - Initially, it is written 'to be a rival,' which implies that neither she nor her rival wife [is permitted]; and then it is written 'to uncover her nakedness,' which implies that only one [of them] is forbidden.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:2.hebrew: במקום מצוה שתיהן אסורין - כדכתיב ״עליה״, דמשמע: במקום ״עליה״:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:2.english: In a place of [a] mitzva, both of them are prohibited - As it is written: “Upon her” [Leviticus 18:18], which implies: in the place of “upon her” [i.e., where the mitzva of levirate marriage applies, as it is written: “Her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her” (Deuteronomy 25:5)].

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:1.hebrew: ואיפוך אנא במקום מצוה היא אסורה וצרתה מותרת - דהא עליה אלגלות ערותה סמיך, דמשמע חדא, למדרש הכי: במקו' עליה הוא דלא אסיר לן אלא חדא, וקרא דלצרור — אשלא במקום מצוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:1.english: And I can reverse [this]: In a place of a mitzvah, she is forbidden and her rival wife is permitted - For behold, “upon her” is adjacent to “to uncover her nakedness,” which implies one [woman], to expound [it] thus: In the place of “upon her” [i.e., levirate marriage], it is that [the Torah] prohibited only one [woman] to us; and the verse’s [phrase] “to be rivals” [applies] to where there is no mitzvah.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:2.hebrew: א"כ לא יאמר עליה - דבלא עליה נמי, כי קשו לן קראי אהדדי, משנינן להו מסברא הכי: היתירא למצוה, ואיסורא שלא במקום מצוה. הלכך, עליה לחדושי אתא — למדרשיה אלצרור, ולמיסר צרה במקום מצוה כערוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:2.english: If so, let [the verse] not say “upon her” - For even without “upon her,” when the verses contradicted each other, we would resolve them by reasoning thus: the permission [applies] to [a place of] the mitzvah, and the prohibition [applies] where there is no mitzvah. Therefore, “upon her” came to innovate — to expound it in connection with “to be a rival” [litzror], and to prohibit the rival wife in a place of the mitzvah just like the forbidden relation.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:8:1.hebrew: ממאי דהאי עליה לאיסורא - אצרה ולא לערוה? דלמא למישרי תרוייהו במקום מצוה אתא, והכי משמע: ואשה אל אחותה לא תקח לצרור — לא היא ולא צרה; ואם עליה דמקום מצוה היא, אפי' בחייה יתקיים (כמו) יבמה יבא עליה דייבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:8:1.english: From where [is it derived] that this “with her” [comes] to prohibit - [applying] to the rival wife and not [only] to the forbidden relative? Perhaps it came to permit both of them in a place of mitzvah, and this is what [the verse] implies: “And a woman to her sister you shall not take, to be a rival” — neither her nor [her] rival wife; and if [it is a case of] “with her” of a place of mitzvah, even in her lifetime it shall be fulfilled (as in) “her brother-in-law shall have intercourse with her” of levirate marriage.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:12:1.hebrew: מאי ולקחה כו' - מצינו למימר דמייתורא דה"א דרשי' תרין ליקוחין, כדדרשינן בפ"ב דקדושין (דף מא.): "ושלח" "ושלחה" — מלמד שהשליח עושה שליח. אבל בקונט' פי' ד"ולקחה" משמע דנפלו לו שתים, ואמר רחמנא: "ולקחה" — לאחת ולא לשתיהן. וליכא להקשות לפירושו: דלמא להא גופא איצטריך, לכשנפלו לו שתי יבמות מבית אחד שלא ייבם אלא אחת — מנא ליה למידרש "כל היכא דאיכא תרין לקוחין כו'"? דהא דרשינן לה בהחולץ (לקמן יבמות דף מד.) מ"את בית אחיו": בית אחד הוא בונה, ואינו בונה שתי בתים. וא"ת: ודלמא אתא קרא למימר שייבם הצרה ולא הערוה? ולמ"ד ערוה לא צריכא קרא — ניחא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:12:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "and he shall take her" [ulekachah], etc. - We could say that from the superfluity of the [letter] heh [at the end of ulekachah] we expound two "takings" [i.e., two options for marriage], just as we expound in the second chapter of Kiddushin (41a): "veshilach" [and he sends] — "veshilchah" [and he sends her] teaches that an agent can appoint [another] agent. However, in the Kuntres [Rashi] he explained that "and he shall take her" implies that two [women] fell to him [for levirate marriage], and the Merciful One said: "and he shall take her" — one [of them], and not both of them. And one cannot object to his explanation [by asking]: Perhaps it is needed for this very [law] itself — when two yevamot fell to him from one house, that he should perform yibum with only one — [so] from where does he know to expound "anywhere that there are two takings, etc."? For we expound that [law] in [the chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 44a) from "his brother's house": he builds one house, and he does not build two houses. And if you ask: Perhaps the verse comes to say that he should perform yibum with the rival wife and not with the forbidden relation? According to the one who says [that a] forbidden relation does not need a verse [to be excluded], this is fine.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:12:2.hebrew: כל היכא דאיכא תרין לקוחין כו' - וא"ת: חייבי עשה נמי ליתסרי לצרה, דליכא למימר "דאי בעי האי נסיב ואי בעי האי נסיב"! ועוד תימה: דהשתא ליכא בצרת ערוה כרת, וא"כ תיבעי חליצה כמו חייבי עשה, דמרבינן להו מיבמתו בפרק שני (לקמן יבמות כ.)! וי"ל: דחייבי עשה, דאיתרבו לחליצה ואית בהו זיקה קצת, הוו בכלל "ולקחה"; וא"כ, צרת ערוה ע"כ לא בעיא חליצה, דאי בעיא, הוי בכלל "ולקחה". ועוד: "ולקחה" משמע לשון תפיסת קידושין; הלכך חייבי עשה, דתפסי בהו קדושין, הוו בכלל "ולקחה":
Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:12:2.english: "Anywhere that there are two [possible] takings, etc." - And if you ask: [Those prohibited by] a positive commandment should also prohibit the rival wife, since one cannot say [in their case] that "if he wants he may marry this one, and if he wants he may marry that one"! And furthermore, it is astonishing: for now [according to this derivation], there is no karet [excision] for the rival wife of a forbidden relation, and if so, she should require chalitzah just like [those prohibited by] a positive commandment, whom we include [as requiring chalitzah] from [the verse] "her brother-in-law" [yevamto] in the second chapter (below, Yevamot 20a)! And one can answer: [Those prohibited by] a positive commandment — since they were included [as subject] to chalitzah and have a slight levirate bond [zikah] — are included in "and he shall take her" [ul'kacha]; and if so, the rival wife of a forbidden relation perforce does not require chalitzah, for if she required [it], she would be included in "and he shall take her." And furthermore: "and he shall take her" implies an expression of betrothal taking effect; therefore, [those prohibited by] a positive commandment, in whom betrothal takes effect, are included in "and he shall take her."

Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:14:1.hebrew: מלמד שמגרשה בגט ומחזירה - בפרק החולץ (לקמן יבמות דף לט.) אמרינן דאיצטריך, דס"ד מצוה דרמא רחמנא עליה עבדה, השתא תיקום עליה באיסור אשת אח. ותימה: דמשמע דלביאה שניה לא צריך קרא להתיר; ואמאי? והא מצוה דרמא רחמנא עליה עבדה מביאה ראשונה, דהא ביאה שניה לא דחיא חייבי לאוין כדאמר בפרק שני (לקמן יבמות כ: ושם). וי"ל: דביאה שניה לא צריכא קרא, דסברא הוא דלא אמר רחמנא יבא עליה לגרשה אחר ביאה ראשונה; ומ"מ ביאה שניה לא דחיא חייבי לאוין, דרשות היא, וליכא עשה אלא בביאה ראשונה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:14:1.english: "[This] teaches that he divorces her with a bill of divorce and remarries her" - In Perek HaCholetz (later, Yevamot 39a), we say that [this verse] is needed, for you might have thought [that since] he has performed the mitzvah that the Merciful One imposed upon him, now she should stand under the prohibition of a brother's wife. And this is puzzling: for it implies that for a second act of intercourse no verse is needed to permit [it]. And why [not]? Behold, he has [already] performed the mitzvah that the Merciful One imposed upon him through the first act of intercourse, for indeed a second act of intercourse does not override [prohibitions of] negative commandments, as stated in the second chapter (later, Yevamot 20b and there). And one can answer: a second act of intercourse does not need a verse, for it is logical that the Merciful One did not say he should come upon her [only] to divorce her after the first act of intercourse; and nevertheless, a second act of intercourse does not override [prohibitions of] negative commandments, for it is optional, and there is no positive commandment except in the first act of intercourse.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:14:2.hebrew: ויבמה בעל כרחה - הכא משמע דמה"א דריש לה. ותימה, דבפ"ק דקידושין (דף יד. ושם) משמע דדריש מה"א ביאה גומר בה ואין כו', דפריך התם: והא מיבעי ליה ויבמה על כרחה, א"כ לימא קרא ויבם! וי"ל, דהתם הכי פריך: א"כ דלביאה גומרת בה גרידא אתא — נימא קרא ויבם! וכענין זה יש לקמן בפרק אלמנה (יבמות דף סח: ושם): א"כ לימא קרא והיא בקדשים לא תאכל. וקשה, לקמן בפ"ב (יבמות דף יט:) דרשינן מיבמה עדיין יבומין הראשונים עליה! וא"ר יצחק, דדרשינן הני תלתא דרשות מיבם ויבם ויבמה; וכענין זה בריש האיש מקדש (קדושין דף מא.) דריש שלשה דרשות מושלחה — שלח ושלח ושלחה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:14:2.english: “And consummate the levirate marriage with her [veyibemah]” — against her will - Here it implies that [the Gemara] derives this from the [final] hei [of veyibemah]. And this is puzzling, for in the first chapter of Kiddushin (14a, and there [in the parallel]) it implies that [the Gemara] derives from the hei that intercourse completes [the acquisition of] her, and not [money or a document], etc., as it asks there: “Isn’t [veyibemah] needed [to teach that he may consummate the levirate marriage with her] against her will? If so, let the verse state veyabem!” And one can answer that there it asks as follows: “If so, that it comes only [to teach] that intercourse completes [the acquisition of] her, let the verse state veyabem!” And similarly, there is [an instance] later in the chapter [entitled] Almanah (Yevamot 68b, and there [in the parallel]): “If so, let the verse state, ‘and she shall not eat of the sacred food.’” And it is difficult, [for] later in the second chapter (Yevamot 19b) we derive from yevamah [that] the first levirate bond is still upon her! And Rabbi Yitzchak says that we derive these three expositions from yabem, veyabem, and veyibemah; and similarly, at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 41a), [the Gemara] derives three expositions from veshilchah — shalach, veshalach, and veshilchah.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:16:1.hebrew: אין חייבין אלא על דבר שזדונו כרת - למעוטי חייבי לאוין. ועל שגגתו חטאת — למעוטי פסח ומילה, דלית בהו חטאת, כדתנן בפ"ק דכריתות (דף ב.). "ולא בעבודת כוכבים אלא על דבר שזדונו כרת" — למעוטי מגפף ומנשק; "ושגגתו חטאת" — למעוטי דבר שאין בו מעשה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:16:1.english: [The court is] obligated only for a matter whose intentional [transgression incurs] karet - [This comes] to exclude those liable for [ordinary] negative commandments. "And whose unwitting [transgression incurs] a sin-offering" — to exclude the Paschal offering and circumcision, for which there is no sin-offering, as we learned in the first chapter of Keritot (2a). "Nor [are they obligated] for idolatry except for a matter whose intentional [transgression incurs] karet" — to exclude one who hugs and kisses [an idol]; "and whose unwitting [transgression incurs] a sin-offering" — to exclude a matter in which there is no action:

Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:1:1.hebrew: למישרי צרה שלא במקום מצוה - וא"ת: להנהו שינויי דלעיל, דמצרכי קרא לערוה גופה — מנא להו למישרי צרה שלא במקום מצוה? וי"ל: דנפקא להו מהיכא דנפקא ליה לרבי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:1:1.english: "To permit a rival wife in a place where the mitzva is not applicable" - And if you say: According to those resolutions above that require a verse for the forbidden relation herself, from where do they derive to permit a rival wife in a place where the mitzva is not applicable? And it can be answered that they derive it from where Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] derives it.
